subject: Recalibrating local anchor multipliers for senior IC offers — proposal
messages:
From: Ariela Soto <ariela@benchmarks.co>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Local-market multipliers — Q2 benchmark set attached

Hi Tessa / Laura,

Attached is the Q2 refresh you asked for: a point-in-time market table built from 6k open offers, active listings and closed comps across SF, NY, SEA, and remote-major markets. Key highlights up front:

- SF senior ICs are showing a 10–18% premium to our current anchor base for comparable IC roles (median ~12%).
- Remote talent pools are compressing: offers clustered within +/-3% of our national anchor.
- London shows a +6% uplift vs our EMEA anchor for specialized infra roles.

Recommendation (concise): adopt a small set of locality multipliers instead of manual one-off exceptions — e.g., SF +12% anchor multiplier, London +6%, Remote +0–3% (role dependent). Implementation notes in the CSV: col"anchor_adj" includes suggested band-edge shifts by level.

Attachments: market-benchmarks-q2-2027.csv

Would you like a 30-min sync today to walk the assumptions? I also included a sample offer sheet for a Senior SWE (Jun Park) showing how base + equity + sign-on would stack with the SF multiplier.

Cheers,
Ariela Soto
Benchmarks Co.
(attachment: market-benchmarks-q2-2027.csv)

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Ariela Soto <ariela@benchmarks.co>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Local-market multipliers — Q2 benchmark set attached

Thanks Ariela — this is the sort of signal we needed. I pulled Jun Park (finalist for Senior SWE) back into the queue and we need to move fast. A few immediate asks and a proposed rule set: 

1) For hiring velocity: approve a temporary locality multiplier table for FY27 hiring cycle (expires 31 Dec 2027) so recruiters can issue offers without VP-level exceptions for single roles. Proposed: SF +12%, London +6%, Remote +0% (unless role is highly scarce).

2) Budget guardrail: individual base increases above band anchor by more than 15% should require Finance notification; >25% requires VP approval — otherwise allow a mix of smaller base uplift + equity top-up.

3) For Jun Park specifically: candidate is in SF, counter from competitor likely at 17% above our anchor. I propose we authorize SF +12% base uplift and a $25k RSU increase to be competitive while preserving comp planning guardrails. Recruiters note: include sign-on if the candidate expects immediate cash.

Can you confirm if this table can be applied programmatically via the offer generator (Workday template) so individual recruiters aren’t forced into manual math on each offer? If yes, I’d like Recruiting to start issuing conditional offers today (subject to final approval form).

Tessa Morgan
Head of Talent, Redwood Inference
(attachment: offer-sheet-senior-engineer.pdf)

Tessa — thank you, Ariela — useful work. A couple of operational guardrails before we roll this out across Recruiting: 

- Headcount impact: our FY27 hiring plan has limited leeway in SF; a straight +12% base uplift across all open SF roles will increase run-rate. We should scope the multiplier to roles identified as at-risk for loss (swe infra, embeddings infra, latency-focused infra).

- Funding levers: prefer to prioritize equity/top-ups before increasing base where possible. For Senior ICs we can approve up to +12% base for up to 6 hires across Q3 if Recruiting flags these as mission-critical and documents competitor loss risk. Anything beyond that should route through Finance for reforecast.

- Approval flow: recommend automatic application of the locality multiplier at recruiter level, but include an automated flag if (base uplift >15% OR total cash comp > 140% of plan) so Compensation team can review.

If we accept that flow, I will draft a short operating note and a one-page decision matrix for managers and recruiters.

Laura Bennett
VP, People Operations

Subject: Approval: one-time SF anchor uplift for Jun Park (HR-4521)

Thanks team — I reviewed the bench data and the headcount constraints. Given the near-term risk to the search and the narrow candidate funnel, I approve the following for Jun Park (Senior SWE):

- Base: apply SF locality multiplier +12% to the published anchor for Senior SWE (one-time application for this offer only).
- Equity: increase RSU grant by $25,000 as Tessa proposed.
- Sign-on: up to $10,000 cash sign-on available if candidate requests.
- Conditions: this uplift is a one-off for candidate Jun Park (HR-4521); Recruiting must record reason in the Workday offer note and route the compensation summary to People Ops for tracking.

Recruiting: please issue the offer with the adjusted numbers. Finance: note for Q3 run-rate reconciliation — k_y_iyer's approval is on file.

Karthik Iyer
SVP, Finance & People Strategy
